items.q: A developer needs to deploy to one resource group but must not see other groups in the subscription. What is the correct approach?
choices: Assign Contributor at the resource-group scope
Assign Reader at the subscription scope
Give them the storage account key
items.explain: RBAC is scoped: Contributor on the single resource group gives deploy rights there and nowhere else — least privilege.

items.q: Which storage redundancy keeps three synchronous copies in one region plus asynchronous copies in a paired region?
items.explain: GRS = 3 sync copies in the primary region + async copies in the paired region. ZRS is zonal within one region.

items.q: You need private connectivity from on-premises to Azure with consistent bandwidth. What do you choose?
items.explain: ExpressRoute is the private dedicated circuit; VPN runs over the public internet.

items.q: An NSG rule allows port 443 from the internet to a VM, but traffic is blocked. What should you check first?
choices: Whether a route table or Azure Firewall overrides the path
items.explain: NSGs are one layer — effective security rules combine NSGs, route tables, and firewalls. Check the whole path.

items.q: Which KQL operator filters rows in Azure Monitor logs?
items.explain: where filters rows; project selects columns; summarize aggregates.

items.q: A VMSS must survive a zone failure in a region with availability zones. What is the minimum zone spread?
choices: Span all zones in the region
items.explain: Zone-redundant VMSS spreads instances across zones — spanning all zones in the region is the resilient pattern.

items.q: A workload needs strong consistency for financial transactions with global distribution. Which Cosmos DB consistency level fits?
items.explain: Strong consistency is the financial-transactions answer; it costs latency and availability — the trade-off is the point.

items.q: RTO is 4 hours and RPO is 1 hour. Which statement is true?
choices: RTO is about data loss, RPO about downtime
RTO is the downtime target, RPO the data-loss target
items.explain: RTO = how fast you're back; RPO = how much data you can lose. Confusing them is the classic exam trap.

items.q: In a hub-and-spoke topology, where does Azure Firewall belong?
choices: In the hub, with user-defined routes from spokes
In the same subnet as the VMs
items.explain: Firewall in the hub, spokes route through it — the canonical forced-tunneling pattern.

items.q: Which migration 'R' means moving a VM as-is to Azure?
items.explain: Rehost = lift and shift. Refactor/rearchitect changes code; replatform tweaks the platform.

items.q: An ADR should record decisions. What else must it record to be useful?
choices: The options considered and why they were rejected
items.explain: An ADR's value is the rejected alternatives and their reasons — that's what future-you needs.

items.q: Active-active across regions primarily buys you what?
choices: Near-zero RTO at higher complexity and cost
items.explain: Active-active minimizes RTO/RPO but doubles operational complexity and cost — the exam tests that trade-off.

items.q: Two VNets with overlapping address spaces need connectivity. What works?
items.explain: Peering requires non-overlapping space. VPN with NAT (or redesign) is the answer — the exam loves this trap.

items.q: You need a web app protected against SQL injection at the edge. Which service?
items.explain: Application Gateway's WAF tier inspects HTTP for OWASP patterns; LB is layer 4 and can't.

items.q: A private endpoint is created for a storage account but the VM resolves the public IP. What's wrong?
choices: The private endpoint is in the wrong region
Private DNS zone missing or not linked to the VNet
The VM needs a public IP
items.explain: Private endpoints need the privatelink DNS zone linked to the VNet — without it, resolution falls back to public.

items.q: ExpressRoute Global Reach connects what?
choices: Two ExpressRoute circuits to each other
items.explain: Global Reach links two ExpressRoute circuits (typically across regions) over Microsoft's backbone.

items.q: Which tool captures packets on an Azure VM without installing anything on it?
choices: Network Watcher packet capture via VM extension
items.explain: Network Watcher's packet capture runs through the VM agent/extension — no manual install on the workload.

items.q: Front Door differs from Traffic Manager primarily in that it is…
choices: An anycast layer-7 reverse proxy with WAF
items.explain: Front Door is anycast L7 with routing rules and WAF; Traffic Manager is DNS-based global load balancing.

items.q: A web tier must survive an AZ failure with no data loss on sessions. What pattern?
choices: Multi-AZ ALB + Auto Scaling + ElastiCache for sessions
items.explain: Stateless web tier across AZs behind an ALB, sessions in ElastiCache — the canonical resilient pattern.

items.q: Which S3 storage class is cheapest for data accessed once a year with millisecond retrieval when needed?
items.explain: Glacier Instant Retrieval: archival pricing with millisecond access. Deep Archive is hours to retrieve.

items.q: An EC2 instance needs S3 access. Best practice?
choices: Embed access keys in the app
Attach an IAM role to the instance
items.explain: IAM roles for EC2 — temporary credentials, no keys to leak.

items.q: Spot Instances are best suited for…
choices: Fault-tolerant batch jobs with flexible timing
items.explain: Spot = interruptible discount compute. Batch, CI, and stateless workers — never the database.

items.q: A company wants to cut EC2 cost for a steady-state workload by ~40% with no architecture change. What first?
items.explain: Savings Plans discount steady-state usage with zero architecture change; Spot needs interruption tolerance.

items.q: Which service decouples microservices with event routing and filtering?
items.explain: EventBridge routes events with rules and filtering; SQS is queueing without routing logic.

items.q: You need an alarm that fires only when two metrics breach together. What do you build?

items.q: Traffic must fail over to a secondary region only when health checks fail. Which Route 53 policy?

items.q: To find idle EC2 instances for rightsizing, what do you check first?

items.q: An application in Account A needs read access to a KMS key in Account B. What is required?
choices: Only an IAM role in Account A
A key policy in Account B granting Account A plus an IAM policy in Account A
items.explain: KMS cross-account needs BOTH: the key policy must trust Account A, and Account A's IAM must allow the use.

items.q: Which S3 feature makes objects immutable for a retention period, even against the root user?
items.explain: Object Lock Compliance mode blocks deletion by anyone, including root, until retention expires.

items.q: GuardDuty reports an EC2 instance mining cryptocurrency. What is the fastest automated containment?
choices: EventBridge rule triggering a Lambda that attaches a quarantine security group
items.explain: Automated quarantine via EventBridge → Lambda is the incident-response pattern the exam expects.

items.q: CloudTrail log file validation primarily protects against what?
items.explain: Digest files let you detect tampered or deleted log files — integrity, not performance.

items.q: A developer's access key was committed to a public repo. What is the FIRST step?
choices: Deactivate/delete the access key, then investigate CloudTrail
items.explain: Kill the credential first, then investigate what it touched in CloudTrail. Order matters.

items.q: SCPs in AWS Organizations are best described as…
items.explain: SCPs filter the maximum allowed — they never grant. Identity policies still grant within the boundary.

items.q: A readiness probe fails while liveness passes. What does OpenShift do?

items.q: Which KQL operator would you use to find sign-ins NOT using MFA?

items.q: In MITRE ATT&CK, credential dumping (OS Credential Dumping) belongs to which tactic?

items.q: Defender XDR's main value over the individual Defender products is…

items.q: A playbook in Sentinel is built on…

items.q: The most important property of a hunting hypothesis is that it is…

items.q: A user signs in from an unusual location on a compliant device with MFA. The risk-based policy should…
choices: Allow — compliant device plus MFA satisfies the policy
items.explain: Conditional Access evaluates combined signals; compliant + MFA is the strong posture the policy was built for.

items.q: Which authentication method is phishing-resistant?
items.explain: FIDO2 binds the credential to the origin — phishing sites can't replay it. SMS/voice/email can be intercepted.

items.q: In OAuth2/OIDC, the ID token primarily tells the app…
items.explain: ID token = identity (OIDC); access token = authorization to call APIs. Mixing them is the classic confusion.

items.q: An on-prem AD user needs SSO to cloud apps without password hash sync. What do you deploy?
items.explain: Pass-through authentication validates against on-prem AD without syncing hashes — the no-hash-sync SSO option.

items.q: PIM's core value for Global Administrators is…
choices: Just-in-time elevation with approval and audit
items.explain: PIM makes privilege temporary, approved, and audited — standing admin is the risk it eliminates.

items.q: An access review finds a contractor with access 6 months after project end. The root cause is…
items.explain: Orphaned access is a lifecycle failure — joiner-mover-leaver automation is the fix, not blame.

items.q: Which format gives the best query cost/performance for analytics on S3?

items.q: A Glue job's schema changes upstream. What prevents silent breakage downstream?

items.q: For exactly-once processing semantics in a streaming pipeline, you need…

items.q: You split data randomly for a time-series forecasting problem. What's wrong?

items.q: For a chatbot needing a foundation model with minimal ML ops, what do you choose?

items.q: Which SageMaker inference option fits unpredictable traffic with long idle periods?

items.q: Hyperparameter tuning with a fixed budget should use…

items.q: The single most important artifact for reproducing an ML experiment is…

items.q: An application needs database credentials that auto-expire. Which Vault engine?
items.explain: Dynamic secrets are generated on demand with leases — expiry is structural, not a calendar reminder.

items.q: A Vault policy grants 'read' on 'secret/data/app/*'. What can't the token do?
choices: Write to those paths or read anything else
items.explain: Policies are deny-by-default least privilege: only the listed capabilities on the listed paths.

items.q: After Vault initialization, what must be protected most carefully?
choices: The unseal key shares and initial root token
items.explain: Unseal shares and the root token are the keys to the kingdom — the ceremony exists for a reason.

items.q: In Consul, health checking determines…
choices: Whether a service instance receives traffic
items.explain: Unhealthy instances leave the catalog/discovery results — health checks are the mesh's truth source.

items.q: Consul 'intentions' control…
choices: Which services may communicate, enforced with mTLS
items.explain: Intentions are L4/L7 allow/deny between services — the zero-trust policy of the mesh.

items.q: Storing production passwords in Consul KV is…
choices: Wrong — KV is for config; secrets belong in Vault
items.explain: Consul KV is not a secrets manager: no dynamic rotation, no lease model. Vault exists for this.

items.q: In Kubernetes, what does etcd store?
choices: The cluster's desired state — all objects
items.explain: etcd is the source of truth for every Kubernetes object. Lose etcd, lose the cluster's memory.

items.q: A Pod's containers share…
choices: Network namespace and optionally storage volumes
items.explain: Pod containers share network (one IP) and can share volumes — the pod is the atomic unit.

items.q: In PromQL, rate(http_requests_total[5m]) computes…
choices: The per-second average rate of increase over 5 minutes
items.explain: rate() over a counter gives per-second increase — the foundation of RED-method alerting.

items.q: A CiliumNetworkPolicy allowing HTTP GET on /api from a labeled client enforces at…
items.explain: Cilium's eBPF datapath enforces L7 policy — beyond what standard NetworkPolicy can express.

items.q: Argo CD detects that live cluster state differs from git. What is this called, and what can Argo do?
choices: Drift; it can auto-sync back to the git state
items.explain: Drift detection with optional auto-sync is GitOps' core loop — the repo stays the truth.

items.q: Signing container images with Cosign primarily defends against…
choices: Tampered or spoofed images in the supply chain
items.explain: Signatures prove the image came from your pipeline untampered — supply-chain security's foundation.
